PullRequest.Title: chore: bump vscode/vsce
PullRequest.Body:

- [x] Verification product build: https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=496941&view=results

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The two serial package-install boundaries and their overlap on libkrb5-dev are explicit in repository code, and the job is explicitly required by pr-gate. Exact elapsed time varies with apt/cache state, but the redundant I/O and critical-path placement do not.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub cache/network transfers, apt metadata downloads, dpkg filesystem operations, and subprocess time
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The duplicate setup runs serially on every Copilot-affecting pull request and merge-group execution selected for chat-lib Linux tests; a cold apt-package cache adds a second apt update/install sequence, while a warm cache still restores and installs the cached .debs before the existing apt sequence.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased required-check latency and unnecessary runner I/O
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The chat-lib Linux job invoked test-chat-lib directly, whose Linux path already runs apt-get update and installs libkrb5-dev once before rebuilding dependencies.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new workflow step first invokes install-linux-packages, which restores or downloads and installs the packages in packages.txt, and then test-chat-lib still unconditionally runs apt-get update and apt-get install -y libkrb5-dev.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The RIGHT-side addition at .github/workflows/pr.yml:1013 inserts install-linux-packages immediately before the unchanged Test chat-lib action, whose Linux implementation already performs apt-get update/install.
Findings.Title: Avoid installing Linux packages twice in the chat-lib job
Findings.Impact: Every Copilot-related PR can spend additional critical-path time restoring/installing the shared nine-package bundle and then refreshing apt metadata/installing Kerberos again before chat-lib can build or test; mirror/cache latency directly delays the required PR gate.
Findings.Evidence: The added line invokes .github/actions/install-linux-packages/action.yml; that action always restores an apt package cache and executes dpkg, or falls back to apt-get update/install. Immediately afterward, .github/actions/test-chat-lib/action.yml lines 32-37 unconditionally execute apt-get update and install libkrb5-dev on Linux. libkrb5-dev is also present in install-linux-packages/packages.txt, and pr-gate lists chat-lib-linux-tests as a required dependency.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep a single Linux package setup: either remove this workflow-level step and retain test-chat-lib's existing Kerberos install, or move the cached package action into test-chat-lib and remove its unconditional apt update/install so all Linux callers install prerequisites exactly once.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot cache-integrity checks on a Copilot-affecting pull request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workspace-image restore, checkout, Node/pnpm setup, the newly added Linux package setup, filtered pnpm install/rebuild/postinstall, and cache checks all complete serially before copilot-check-test-cache can pass; the PR gate waits for this job.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore the apt-package cache, or run apt-get update/install on a miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cache lookup/restore per selected job; on a cold cache, one apt metadata refresh and one installation for the fixed nine-package list
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This job proceeded directly from pnpm setup to the filtered dependency install and had no apt-package cache or apt boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before dependency installation and cache checks begin

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dpkg invocation containing all cached packages missing from the runner image
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No system-package filesystem installation occurred in this job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serial setup on a warm apt cache

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install the filtered Copilot/chat-lib dependency graph with pnpm
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One filtered install plus one filtered rebuild; cold store downloads changed packages, warm image/store reuses them
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same install/rebuild commands ran against VSCE 3.6.0 and the previous lock graph.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing critical-path setup before cache validation

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One job per selected PR or merge-group run; the system package set is fixed at nine entries, while pnpm work scales with changed packages in the filtered Copilot/chat-lib dependency graph.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The package-cache restore/dpkg or apt fallback is serial before pnpm. pnpm rebuild may build package internals concurrently, but no workflow-level overlap shortens this job's critical path; sibling CI jobs run independently in parallel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: With a warm workspace image, pnpm reuses node_modules/store but still checks the filtered graph. With a warm apt-package cache, the new action restores cached .debs and runs dpkg; on a miss it performs apt-get update/install. There is no coalescing across concurrently running jobs because each runner restores and installs independently.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the new cache/apt/dpkg boundaries are serial and diff-introduced; insufficient evidence that they are avoidable in this job.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact package-cache hit rate and runner-image package baseline are unknown, so the added duration is uncertain; no second setup sequence exists in this job and the changed lock resolution provides a plausible native-build prerequisite.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the new setup adds bounded CI work, but unlike the chat-lib job it does not duplicate an existing package-install boundary, and repository comments tie the filtered rebuild path to Linux headers.

Scenarios.Scenario: chat-lib Linux build and test on a Copilot-affecting pull request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workspace restore and checkout are followed by the new shared Linux package action, then test-chat-lib performs its own Linux apt setup before filtered installs, extraction, build, and tests. The required PR gate waits for the job.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore cached .debs or fetch apt metadata/packages for the shared nine-package list
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new package-cache restore, or one apt update/install pair on a miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The job invoked test-chat-lib directly and did not run this shared package action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dpkg invocation on a warm cache for all runner-missing packages
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serial before the existing apt setup

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh apt metadata and install libkrb5-dev
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unconditional apt-get update and one apt-get install per Linux invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was the single Linux package setup; after the diff it repeats package setup and overlaps on libkrb5-dev.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks pnpm rebuild and all chat-lib build/test work

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Filtered pnpm installs and rebuilds for Copilot and extracted chat-lib
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two filtered installs and one rebuild, with downloads only for cold/missing store content
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same dependency-install sequence followed the single Kerberos setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing critical path after package setup

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Linux chat-lib job per selected PR or merge group; package work is a fixed shared nine-package bundle plus the repeated Kerberos installation check.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two package-install sequences execute serially in the same job. Other Copilot jobs may run in parallel, but they do not coalesce apt metadata, cache downloads, or dpkg work across runners.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm shared apt cache changes the first sequence from apt network access to cache restore plus dpkg; a miss performs apt-get update/install. In both cases test-chat-lib then unconditionally performs apt-get update and apt-get install for libkrb5-dev, so the overlap remains. Workspace/pnpm caches do not eliminate either system setup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high confidence: both setup sequences are explicit, serial, and on a required job path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mirror and cache latency varies, but the duplicate serial boundary is unconditional and libkrb5-dev is explicitly present in both package lists.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated I/O regression; finding submitted at .github/workflows/pr.yml:1013.

Scenarios.Scenario: Package Copilot VSIX and enumerate built-in/mobile extension files with VSCE 4.1.1
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For Copilot packaging, pnpm deploy stages production dependencies and a Node subprocess runs VSCE package. Built-in and mobile packaging call VSCE listFiles, then read/copy selected files. These operations are build/package critical paths, not editor startup or runtime paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run pnpm deploy and then VSCE package for the Copilot extension
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pnpm subprocess and one Node/VSCE subprocess per requested VSIX package
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subprocess sequence used VSCE 3.6.0.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both must complete before the VSIX exists

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate VSCE-selected files and read/copy them into mobile artifacts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One listFiles call per configured mobile extension and one read/write per selected source file
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same calls and cardinality used VSCE 3.6.1.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serial per extension after browser builds; required for artifact completion

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate and stream files for built-in extensions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One listFiles call per packaged built-in extension and one stat/read stream per returned file
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same repository call path used VSCE 3.6.1.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install VSCE and its transitive dependencies from the pnpm store/registry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One package-manager resolution per install root; cold stores download the changed graph, warm stores reuse content, and optional native keyring packages select by platform
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Dependency installation already occurred for VSCE 3.6.x; the lock graph replaces keytar/secretlint tooling with the VSCE 4.1.1 graph.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dependency installation precedes packaging, but is not repeated per source file

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Copilot cost scales with staged dependency and extension file counts; built-in/mobile cost scales with each packaged extension's source files. The diff changes the VSCE implementation/version but not caller count or input cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Copilot staging and VSCE packaging are serial. Mobile manifests and initial reads use Promise.all, then extensions are copied sequentially; built-in extension streams are managed by existing build orchestration. The diff adds no new fan-out or limiter change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Node module resolution is warm after install; VSCE file enumeration operates on the filesystem without a repository-level result cache. pnpm deploy reuses the pnpm store when warm and downloads on a cold store. The version bump does not alter explicit cache keys or invalidation in repository code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the unchanged call paths and cardinalities; low confidence in any adverse runtime delta from the package version alone.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No benchmark or dependency source is available to establish that VSCE 4.1.1 performs more filesystem/CPU work for the same inputs; the lockfile also removes many old transitive packages, so install/package magnitude cannot be inferred as a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff changes dependency implementation but does not prove added boundary calls, hotter placement, increased cardinality, or retained state in repository code.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all eight changed files and complete lockfile diff pages. The VSCE dependency bump does not establish a packaging/runtime performance regression by itself. One concrete CI regression was found: chat-lib Linux now performs two serial system-package setup sequences on a required PR-gate path.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
